parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation or documented targeting of trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is lawful, marriage/civil partnerships have overwhelming local support, legal gender change has existed since 2014, and parent-issued gender recognition certificates are recognised — positive climate signals. Visitor-facing gaps remain: no gender-identity ground in anti-discrimination or hate-crime provisions, no nonbinary recognition, and no sourced evidence on border treatment, facilities, custody, or trans-specific violence and police practice. Those absences are largely resident-facing gaps or open questions, not documented exposures, and should not be treated as proof of danger. But the territory is small and the visitor-specific record is thin, so silence is not strong safety evidence either. Reduced risk, below jurisdictions with documented acceptance plus operating visitor protections.
